details:
Scenario

According to the Food and Angriculture Organization, “33 percent of global soils are already degraded”. This is caused by monoculture where same crop is grown years on end. As a result millions of people around the world are losing time and money. The solution is crop rotation . During a study by the University of Nebraska, it was found that there was a “[decrease in] crop losses [caused] drought by 14-90%”. With that being said, farmers are still left wondering what are the effective rotation strategies for their region.


Solution

Zoe is a website that utilizes live NASA Power weather data for a given location to produce effective rotation strategy. Farmers select region on a map and choose their priority among water conservation, soil quality, and foraging. Data and weights go into a system of lightweight models that test the region using information from 7 additional datasets

Differences

Existing Solutions:

Check average of all years in normal conditions

Broad data regions (not specific)

Factors like heat, frost, drought are measured separately

Long and convoluted analysis

ZOE:

Focuses on the worst possible year for a given region

Polygon drawing tool to draw specific region

Combination of factors are tested like Heat + Drought

Easy to understand output with visuals
